decisions.reason: The organic sliced ham is part of an announced organic line that fits the firm's strategic direction toward organic meats, and the firm has committed to it publicly, so management is likely to persist even without later evidence of success.

The organic Kasseler belongs to the same organic range the firm committed to, so dropping it would undercut the announced direction, though it is a smaller niche item and more vulnerable than the ham.
The organic pepper salami is central to the organic expansion, and any weak sales can be blamed on temporary pandemic-era market disruptions, which favours keeping it.

The exotic teriyaki aspic for the service counter was a showcased creation, but deli counters suffered during the pandemic; that setback can be framed as temporary, so management likely keeps it despite elevated risk.
The fennel salami received a dedicated product page, which signals strong visible commitment, so management will likely persist with it.
The classic veal liver pâté fits the firm's core assortment, needed little specific investment, and is likely to sell steadily, so keeping it is the natural choice.
